ai.title: Fix Anthropic tool call ordering
ai.summary: Refactored agent runtime to collect tool calls and results in `toolCallsToAddToMessageHistory` and `toolResultsToAddToMessageHistory` arrays instead of pushing directly to `messageHistory` or using `toolResultsToAddAfterStream`. This ensures correct interleaved ordering of assistant tool calls and tool results in the message history, fixing bugs with Anthropic's strict tool call/result pairing requirements. Scope covers `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-programmatic-step.ts`, `tool-stream-parser.ts`, `tools/stream-parser.ts`, and `tools/tool-executor.ts`. Tool calls are now pushed to `toolCallsToAddToMessageHistory` only when `excludeToolFromMessageHistory` is false, and results similarly gated, replacing the previous `skipDirectResultPush` flag.

eli5.text: When you asked the Agent for a task and it decided to use a tool (like searching files or running code), the assistant would now and then send the tool request to Anthropic in the wrong order, like handing in a recipe before you're even asked to bake. To fix that, the system now gathers up its tool requests and the replies it gets back, then lines them up in the correct order before it shows the final sequence to the assistant. This only matters when an assistant is actively running a programmatic step with tools enabled, and you would only see the effect if you were watching a multi-turn session that relies on Anthropic's strict tool call and result pairing. It is live today across the agent runtime's step and tool-streaming paths.

ai.title: SDK 0.10.5 fixes missing tool calls
ai.summary: sdk/CHANGELOG.md adds 0.10.5 entry documenting fix for missing tool calls and results. 0.10.4 entry notes various agent runtime improvements. Scope limited to @codebuff/sdk package changelog.

eli5.text: The assistant no longer drops instructions it was supposed to follow (the ones that tell it to call tools or use external services). You would notice by checking: things that used to sometimes not happen now happen reliably. Developers who depend on the assistant working with other software will see fewer errors where the assistant just stopped mid-task. It's like fixing a dropped phone call where one side stopped hearing the other.

ai.title: SDK 0.10.5
ai.summary: Bumped the @codebuff/sdk package version from 0.10.4 to 0.10.5, shipping the Anthropic tool call ordering fix, new model support, and minor CLI/ad-panel updates. The version field in sdk/package.json is the only change in this commit, with the full release content detailed in the surrounding 0.10.5 updates.
ai.evidence: sdk/package.json: version field changed from '0.10.4' to '0.10.5' in the @codebuff/sdk package manifest. The accompanying release ships the Anthropic tool call ordering fix in packages/agent-runtime (run-programmatic-step.ts, tool-stream-parser.ts, tools/stream-parser.ts, tools/tool-executor.ts) and adds claude-opus-4.6, kimi-k2.5, and glm-4.7 to the agent ModelName union via agents/agent-definition.ts, alongside CLI ad info panel (cli/src/components/ad-banner.tsx) and grant-credits.ts script

eli5.text: Freebuff SDK 0.10.5 adds support for three powerful new AI models, fixes frustrating tool-calling bugs, and gives you control over the ads you see in the terminal. You can now use Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6, Moonshot's Kimi K2.5, and Zhipu's GLM 4.7 as the brains behind your AI agents, while fixes to the agent runtime ensure tool calls and results appear in the correct order so tasks no longer get skipped or jumbled. The CLI's ad banner now shows an information panel when you click on the ad label and includes a disable button, so free users can opt out of sponsored content or learn more about what they're seeing. Developers managing team accounts receive a new internal script for quickly granting compute credits to users, which streamlines onboarding and support workflows. Upgrading gives you access to the latest model capabilities and eliminates the missing-step errors that could cause complex multi-tool operations to break silently.

ai.title: Wrap markdown table cells instead of truncating
ai.summary: Replaced truncateText with wrapText in cli/src/utils/markdown-renderer.tsx to enable word-wrapping for table cells. The renderTable function now calculates row heights based on wrapped content, ensuring long text remains visible across multiple lines rather than being cut off with an ellipsis. This change affects CLI markdown rendering, specifically table layouts.

eli5.text: When a table with long text in its cells is printed to your terminal, the text no longer gets cut off with dots at the end. Instead, the text now wraps onto multiple lines so you can read the entire content without anything being hidden. This makes tables easier to read when they contain lengthy descriptions or data.

ai.title: Filter orphaned tool calls on abort in stream-parser
ai.summary: Added logic to filter out tool calls without corresponding tool results when the signal is aborted in `processStream`. Prevents provider errors like "unexpected tool_use_id found in tool_result blocks" caused by race conditions where tool calls are added synchronously but results arrive asynchronously. Scope limited to `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/stream-parser.ts`. Uses a `Set` of completed tool call IDs to verify existence before appending to message history.

eli5.text: When an assistant is interrupted mid-task (aborted), it used to send incomplete tool usage records to its response system, which the system didn't understand and rejected with an error. Now, it checks that every tool action it references actually has a matching result before including it, avoiding the confusion. You would notice fewer errors appearing when the assistant is stopped or interrupted during a task. This fix is live today.

ai.title: Remove hardcoded tier description from Stripe subscription
ai.summary: Removed hardcoded `description` field from `subscription_data` in `web/src/app/api/stripe/create-subscription/route.ts`. Eliminates static tier pricing text from Stripe API payload.

eli5.text: The pricing label that used to appear next to paid subscriptions created through the Codebuff sign-up flow has been removed, so new subscriptions no longer carry a fixed description like "Codebuff Strong, $X/mo" in Stripe. The change is live now and only affects subscriptions created from the main subscription-creation endpoint; Stripe metadata and billing tiers themselves are untouched, so existing subscribers notice no change and new ones simply won't see that extra text. If you checked a freshly created subscription in Stripe's dashboard, the description field would just be blank now. This is a small maintenance tweak the team rated as minor.

eli5.text: A behind-the-scenes menu in the app that changed your subscription plan was removed because nothing was using it anymore. No one should notice anything different, it only affected how the app talked to Stripe (the payment system), and since that conversation already moved to a different path months ago, deleting the old code fixes no live behavior. Your subscription, billing cycle, and ability to upgrade or downgrade remain unchanged today.

ai.title: Claude subscription deprecation notice
ai.summary: CLI banners and slash command labels now display deprecation warnings for Claude subscription support. FAQ updated with removal date and ban reports. Scope: `claude-connect-banner.tsx`, `slash-commands.ts`, `faq.mdx`. Migration path: `/subscribe` to Codebuff Strong.

eli5.text: Starting today, anyone who has connected their paid Claude account (Pro or Max) to Codebuff will see a new warning in the app’s main screen and beside the /connect:claude command: the link to use that subscription will be cut off on March 1st. The help page repeats the same cutoff date and adds that some users have reported being blocked by Anthropic after heavy use through Codebuff, advising people to run the /subscribe command to move to a Codebuff Strong plan instead.
